title: Wagon cup holder: v7.1, stronger strut grip
subtitle: Ring on the side rail + a C-grip on the angled strut · no screw · the clip and the cup lift off together for folding · shown assembled in its real orientation (rail left to right, strut end on the left) · millimetres

meshes.label: Clip (ring on rail + grip on strut; pops off)
Angled strut (13.5 mm square, nominal gap 5.5 mm)

scale_note: Real size, shown assembled in its real orientation: the rail runs left to right, the cup stands upright and hangs off the outside of it. The rail is your 22.3 mm tube; the angled strut is your 13.5 mm square bar, drawn as a straight line at ~59° from the tape photos (so it is accurate to roughly a few mm). The gap between the rail and the strut is the least certain number (4 to 7 mm, drawn at 5.5). The tumbler is from retailer listings. The wireframe blocks are the red latch zones (approximate).
notes_title: What changed, and what to check
notes: v7.1: the v7 clip fit well but its strut grip let go under a full cup. The cup's weight pushes the strut toward the grip's mouth, so the lips are what hold it. The lips are now 1.6 mm deep (was 1.0) on 3 mm walls (was 2.5), the clearance is 0.3 mm (was 0.4) and the grip is 22 mm long (was 18), which I estimate roughly triples the holding force. Only the clip changes: your printed module still fits. Please check: (1) the grip section (cup side to the right): lips wrap the strut's outer face; (2) print the new grip test (three lip depths: 1.6 / 2.0 / 2.4 mm = 16 / 20 / 24 mm tall) and tell me which holds under a pull but still goes on by hand; (3) which snap let go before, the strut grip or the ring on the bar?
